requests.text: Where meaningful reading of the plaint identifies a substantive tenancy-continuance or tenancy-term controversy, those questions are for civil-court adjudication rather than determination as a Section 50 trust-affairs inquiry.
requests.submitted_text: The Supreme Court's identified controversy over tenancy continuance, terms and duration is a subject for civil adjudication rather than determination as a Section 50 trust-affairs inquiry. This procedural subject-matter conclusion does not establish the existence, validity, duration or continued operation of the plaintiffs' asserted tenancy.

requests.text: A genuine trust-affairs inquiry prayer is treated under Section 50 and the applicable Section 51 consent regime rather than being converted into an ordinary tenancy question.
requests.submitted_text: The distinct prayer for inquiry into alleged trust misconduct follows the Section 50 trust-affairs route and the applicable Section 51 consent regime. This classification neither proves trust misconduct nor establishes whether the required consent was sought or obtained.

requests.text: When a whole-plaint review identifies a civil-adjudicable tenancy subject alongside a separate special-Act trust-inquiry prayer, the mere combination of those prayers does not itself justify rejecting the entire plaint; lawful restriction to tenancy issues and applications to relinquish other prayers are distinct procedural matters.
requests.submitted_text: The presence of a special-Act trust-inquiry prayer alongside a civil-adjudicable tenancy controversy does not alone justify rejection of the whole plaint under Order VII Rule 11(a) or (d). This does not foreclose another properly established whole-plaint ground for rejection or prove that any requested remedy must be granted.

requests.text: Continuation of the tenancy issue does not decide the reserved possession or injunction merits; a forcible-possession plea may be raised and considered only insofar as relevant to the continued suit.
requests.submitted_text: The procedural availability of civil adjudication concerning tenancy does not establish forcible dispossession, a right to restoration under Section 6 of the Specific Relief Act, or entitlement to an injunction. The disputed possession event and the separate discretionary injunction questions remain matters for relevant evidence and appropriate merits assessment. This is an analytically supported distinction, not a completed mechanical evaluation or a substantive merits ruling.
